items.title: Louis Barbarin Interview, 1960-06-22
items.q: an organized band named Imperial Serenaders gave me my break. I played with them around here a while. And they'd taken a job at the Victory Inn, a night spot on the Jefferson Highway. Albert Snider, the trumpet man who was in charge of the band, had a day job.

ctx.x: I learned drums by playing on my mother's chairs, the two forks. That was in the year of 1916. My father bought my brother, Paul, a set of drums. And Paul was playing around here with different bands. And he was called to Chicago to play with Manuel Ferrer's band at the Royal Garden in Chicago. My first set of drums was the one Paul was working with in Chicago. And he sent them to me because he bought some new ones. Well, I was on the way to start playing the first job. I played a house party, just a piano and…
I don't believe you gave us your birth date exactly. And just what part of the city you were born in. I didn't want that. Right at the very beginning. Okay. I was born in New Orleans.
